record.original_question: For a Pinwheel tiling of the plane, place a point mass at the natural reference point of each tile and consider the resulting Dirac comb. Its diffraction measure is the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation and is known to have circular symmetry. Determine where the sharp rings occur in this diffraction measure and compute their intensities.

evidence.quote: A Pinwheel Tiling is then defined as a tiling of the plane whose tiles are isometric copies of T, in which a tile may intersect another tile only either on a whole side or on half the length 2 side, and such that the following property holds : the tiles of any Pinwheel Tiling can be grouped in sets of five into homothetic tiles, so that these homothetic tiles form (up to rescaling) a new Pinwheel Tiling.

Choose a reference point (a natural choice is the point at coordinates (1/2, 1/2) with respect to the vertex point at the right–angled corner of the triangular tile) and consider a uniform Dirac comb obtained by placing a point measure at each reference point. The diffraction measure is the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation and is a well–defined positive measure.

There are arguments that support the existence of such ‘sharp rings’ in the diffraction measure of the pinwheel tiling ... However, none of these properties has yet been proved. Problem 2.3.1. Determine the position of sharp rings in the diffraction measure of a Pinwheel Tiling and their intensity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let T be the right triangle with legs of lengths 1 and 2 (and hypotenuse √5). A Pinwheel Tiling of the Euclidean plane R^2 is a tiling whose tiles are isometric copies of T such that any two tiles meet either along an entire side or along exactly half of a side of length 2, and which admits a hierarchical structure: the tiles can be grouped into sets of five forming homothetic copies of T which themselves (after rescaling) form a Pinwheel Tiling.

Fix a Pinwheel Tiling and, in each tile, place a point at the position with coordinates (1/2, 1/2) measured from the right-angled vertex (with respect to the legs as coordinate axes). Let Λ ⊂ R^2 be the resulting point set, and let ω = Σ_{x ∈ Λ} δ_x be the associated Dirac comb. Define the autocorrelation
  γ = lim_{R → ∞} (1/|B_R|) (ω|_{B_R} ∗ \tilde{ω}|_{B_R}),
where \tilde{ω}(A) = ω(−A), B_R is the ball of radius R, and the limit is taken in the vague topology (it exists for the Pinwheel Tiling). The diffraction measure of the tiling is the Fourier transform \hat{γ}, a positive translation-bounded measure on R^2; it is known to be circularly symmetric (invariant under all rotations about the origin).

Determine explicitly:
(a) the set of radii r > 0 at which \hat{γ} has a singular component supported on the circle {ξ ∈ R^2 : |ξ| = r} (the "sharp rings"), and
(b) the intensity (mass) of \hat{γ} carried on each such circle.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact positions and intensities of the sharp rings in the diffraction measure of the Pinwheel Tiling remain unresolved. The diffraction is known to be circularly symmetric with a Bragg peak of unit intensity at the origin, and there is strong heuristic and numerical evidence for further sharp rings, but their precise locations and intensities have not been rigorously determined. Recent work (e.g., "Circles in diffraction", 2024) develops tools toward computing such ring intensities for statistically circularly symmetric substitution tilings, but a complete answer for the pinwheel case has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Some comments on pinwheel tilings and their diffraction
status_evidence.snippet: Pinwheel diffraction is circularly symmetric and consists of sharp rings and possibly a continuous component; precise positions/intensities not established.
status_evidence.claim: Status of pinwheel diffraction: rings exist with strong evidence but are not rigorously characterized.

status_evidence.title: Circles in diffraction (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: A method for computing the intensity of a circle in the diffraction is developed as a new tool for substitution tilings with statistical circular symmetry such as the pinwheel.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress toward computing ring intensities, indicating the pinwheel problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Pinwheel tiling - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The diffraction is rotationally invariant; beyond the central Bragg peak little is rigorously known.
status_evidence.claim: Open status of full diffraction structure of pinwheel tilings.
